दिनांक 24.10.2021 को
माननीय प्र धानमंत्ी श् ी नरेंद्र मोदी जी
मन की बात कार्यक्रम में बीपीआरण्डडी की पुस्तक डोपो का संिर्य िेते हु ए।
पुलिस सेवा से जुड़ी एक और बात जो मैं मन की बात के श् ोताओं को
बताना चाहता हं कक पहिे यह धारणा बन गई थ़ी सेना और पुलिस
जैस़ी सेवा केवि पुरुषों के लिए होत़ी है िेककन आज ऐसा नहीं है ब्यू रो
ऑफ पुलिस ररसच्च एंड डेविपमेंट के आंकडे बताते हैं कक पपछिे कुछ वषषों
में मपहिा पुलिस करममि यों की संख्ा दोगुऩी हो गई है। 2014 में जहां इनकी
संख्ा 1,05,000 के कऱीब थ़ी वहीं 2020 तक इसमें दोगुने से भ़ी ज् ादा
की बढोतऱी हु ई है और यह संख्ा 2,15,000 तक पहुंच गई है यहां तक की
सेंट्रि आरड्च पुलिस फोस्चस में भ़ी पपछिे 7 सािों में मपहिाओं की संख्ा
िगभग दोगुऩी हु ई है।

INTRODUCTION
SECTION I : DATA COLLECTION TECHNIQUE

This section provides information regarding the purpose of publication, user guide to
Indian Police Statistics, data source and quality, statistical tools, the procedure of data collection,
limitations, and implications.
PURPOSE OF PUBLICATION
The BPR&D has been publishing the “Data on Police Organizations” in India since 1986,
annually. From time to time, some of the essential features like woman police, police expenditure,
constabulary ratio, transport facilities, communication facilities, representation of SCs/STs, and
police training institutes were added.
```
In this publication, dimensions like the infrastructure of CAPFs (vehicle availability, family
```
```
quarters, training institutions, tracker and sniffer dogs, and pay scales), Gender- wise data on
```
CHAPTER11
40Promoting Good Practices & Standards
CHAPTER 1 | INTRODUCTION
Police Forces, District Armed Reserve Police, Senior Supervisory Officers, Immediate Supervisory
Officers, and Field Staff Ratio, Data of Woman Police, Sanctioned and Actual Strength of SCs/STs
and OBCs have been added.
This issue of “Data on Police Organizations” in India, as on 01.01.2021, will be more beneficial
for the users, especially for the policymakers, police officers, researchers, academicians, police
administrators, and other stakeholders, as it is coming out timely.
DATA COLLECTION PROCEDURE
```
“Data on Police Organizations” in India (DoPO) has been prepared based on the data
```
provided by the States/UTs, CAPFs, and other Central Police Organizations. Further, data have
```
also been obtained from the Registrar General of India (RGI) and the Survey of India (SOI).
```
STATISTICAL TOOLS
Statistical methods involved in carrying out the study include planning, designing,
collecting data, analyzing, drawing meaningful interpretation, and reporting the findings.
PRESENTATION OF DATA
Data are collected in a raw format. Therefore, data have been summarized, processed,
analyzed, and presented in charts and tables to make them more meaningful. However, in this
format, there are inherent difficulties in its understanding.
The graph is a very effective visual tool. It displays data at a glance, facilitates comparison,
reveals trends and relationships within the data, such as changes over time, frequency distribution
and correlation, etc. Bar graphs, Pie charts, and other statistical tools have been used.
DATA LIMITATIONS
DoPO has been prepared based on data provided by the States/UTs/CAPFs and other
Police Organizations.
Police structures in different States/UTs, CAPFs, and CPOs are not uniform. In a few cases,
```
States/UTs have not provided complete data; consequently, it has been mentioned as ‘Not
```
```
Available (NA)/Not Provided (NP)’ in the relevant Tables and, at places, wherever appropriate,
```
data of the previous year has been incorporated for the sake of comparison.

CHAPTER 1 | INTRODUCTION
SECTION II: INDIAN DEMOGRAPHY
 Male & Female Population
 Geographical Area
This section depicts the information/data of States/UTs regarding demography, containing
the country’s male-female population and geographical area.
MALE & FEMALE POPULATION
Demography is the statistical study of populations, especially human beings. At a glance,
it analyzes living population, i.e., changes over time and space in response to birth, migration,
aging, death, etc.
Its analysis covers entire society or groups defined by education, nationality, religion,
ethnicity, etc. Demographic studies also analyze the relationships between economic, social,
cultural, and biological processes influencing the population.
The total population of India, as on 01.10.2020, as provided by the Registrar General of
India and the Census Commissioner of India, is 135.69 crore, approx., comprising 69.79 crore
males and 65.9 crore females.
Among the States, Uttar Pradesh, with a population of more than 22.96 crores, is the most
populous state in the country, followed by Maharashtra, with a population of 12.39 crore.
Among the Union Territories, Delhi, with a population of more than 2.04 crore, is the most
populous UT in the country, followed by J&K, with a population of 1.33 crore.
GEOGRAPHICAL AREA
The total geographical area of the country is 32,87,162 Sq. Kms, approximately. In terms
of geographical area, the largest state in India is Rajasthan, with an area of 3,42,111 sq. Km. and
the smallest is the UT of Lakshadweep, with an area of 30 sq. Km.

visible at the cutting edge level.

MODERNIZATION GRANTS TO THE STATE POLICE FORCES
Modernization grants to the state police forces, allocated by the MHA, are meant to upgrade
the infrastructure of the state police in order to improve their capacity to meet the emerging
challenges of internal security, besides improving efficiency and effectiveness in Police service
delivery.
The focus of the scheme is on strengthening of the police infrastructure by way of
construction of secure and people friendly Police Stations, Police Outposts, Police Housing,
improved Mobility, Modern Weaponry, Computerization, Communication Equipment, Modern
Traffic Control Equipment etc.
At the national level, the grants made available to the state police forces in the financial
year 2020-21 by the Central Government and the State Governments and the total amount
utilized for modernization by the State Governments for the State Police Forces are given at
Table No - 4.1.4.

```
TRANSPORT FACILITIES (MOBILITY)
```
Mobility is measured in terms of the availability of vehicles to move the unit on the call
of duty. Police mobility is directly linked with its operational efficiency. During law and order
situations, the quick response of police forces helps significantly in protecting the life and
property of the people.
Vehicles required to provide mobility to Police Forces have been divided into four categories,
```
i.e., Heavy Vehicles (buses/trucks, troop carriers, etc.), Medium Vehicles, Light Vehicles (jeeps/
```
```
cars, etc.), and Very Light Vehicles (three/two Wheelers). Heavy, Medium and Light vehicles cater
```
to the requirements of the Police Stations and field-level supervisory and senior supervisory
officers.
Besides above, State Police have also procured some special purpose vehicles: like Mines
```
Protected Vehicles (MPV), Riot Control Vehicles, Ambulances, Mobile Forensic Vans, Water
```
Cannons, Water Tankers, Prison Vans, etc., to meet their specific needs. These vehicles have
been clubbed under the “ Other Category ”.
```
In all, 2,07,030 vehicles were available with State/UT Police Force in 2020; This number
```
increased from 2,02,925 during 2019. Out of 2,03,070 vehicles, 11,491 are Heavy-duty Vehicles,
```
17,399 Medium-duty Vehicles, 87,123 Light Vehicles, 89,502 Very Light Vehicles (two/three-
```
```
wheelers) and 1,499 are Other Vehicles (Table No-5.1.6).
```

This section provides State/UT wise data on CCTV cameras, computers, servers and laptops,
speedometers, breath analyzers, and forensic science laboratories/mobile forensic science vans
available with the Police.
Police human resources alone are insufficient to curb crime, maintain law and order,
traffic management, internal security, and other policing requirements. Therefore, they must
be supplemented with modern facilities and gadgets like computers, CCTV cameras, traffic and
investigation equipment, speedometers, breath analyzers, forensic science kits/labs, etc., to
enhance effectiveness and efficiency.
```

(MFSVs)

and compiled on 01.01.2021. At the national level, 642 Forensic Science Laboratories (FSLs)/

MFSVs are available, out of which 32 are main laboratories, 81 are regional laboratories, and the
```
remaining 529 are mobile laboratories (Table No - 6.1.1).

CENTRAL ARMED POLICE FORCES(CAPFs) DEPLOYED IN THE STATES/UTs
```
```
A total of 1,999 Central Armed Police Forces (BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP, SSB, etc.) were deployed
```
```
on Internal Security duties in different States/UTs for more than six months during 2020 (Table
```
```
No - 6.1.7).
```
The deployment of the Central Armed Police Forces in the States/UTs had shown a steady
increase from 2012 to 2014 but has declined after that, as shown in the graph.
Further, through the analysis of the deployment of 1,999 companies of CAPFs, it is observed
that 703 companies of CAPFs were deployed in Jammu and Kashmir, followed by 292 companies
in Chhattisgarh. It indicates that the country’s North, Central, and North Eastern regions, which
are affected with Terrorism/Left Wing Extremism, Insurgency had a significant deployment of
CAPFs during the period.

 Police Personnel Recruited

```
This section contains the data from States/UTs in respect of Police Personnel (Constables
```
```
and SIs) recruited during the year 2020 and the number of newly recruited police personnel
```
who underwent training.
POLICE PERSONNEL RECRUITED
The 72,520 Police Constables were recruited during 2020 against the 1,05,353 recruited
in 2019. At the State level, the highest number of 49,699 Constables were recruited in UP,
```
followed by 8,773 in Tamil Nadu (Table No - 6.1.8).
```
```
The number of Sub-Inspectors (SIs) recruited during 2020 was 8,503, whereas this figure
```
was 12,909 during 2019. At the State level, the highest number of SIs recruited were 6,151 in
```
UP, followed by 1,531 in West Bengal (Table No - 6.1.8).
```
TRAINING OF NEWLY RECRUITED POLICE PERSONNEL
```
Total 1,01,944 newly recruited Police Personnel from Constables to the Dy SP (Civil, District
```
```
Armed Reserve, and Special Armed police) were trained during 2020 in State Police Training
```
Institutes. The break-up is 80,077 Constables, 5,885 Head Constables, 2,194 ASI, 11,220 SIs,
```
745 Dy.SP and 1823 Any others (Table No - 6.1.10).
```
The highest number, i.e., 3,284 SIs, were trained by the Jharkhand Police, followed by 1609
SIs by Bihar. As far as Constables are concerned, 14,700 Constables were trained in UP, followed
by 10,690 from Bihar.
Promoting Good Practices & Standards75
CHAPTER 6 | POLICE INFRASTRUCTURE
IPS OFFICERS
The sanctioned strength of IPS Officers, as on 01.01.2021, was 4,984 at the all- India level,
whereas 4,102 officers are available. Further, 387 IPS Officers were on deputation with the
```
Central Government (Table No. 6.2.2).
```
POLICE TRAINING INSTITUTES
Regular and adequate training of Police Personnel at all levels is necessary to upgrade
their professional knowledge, skills, and attitude and instill confidence and professionalism
in the Police Personnel. It contains information about Police Training Institutes of the States/
UTs and CAPFs. These institutions cater to the basic training of the newly recruited Police
Personnel, in-service training to Police Personnel of different ranks: specialized training to the
```
Police Personnel deployed for specialized work and assignments like Special Task Force (STF),
```
```
Special Investigation Teams (SITs), Commandos, etc. Some of these Training Institutes have been
```
recognized as the “Centre of Excellence” for imparting specialized training in a particular field/
craft/ trade.
STATE TRAINING INSTITUTES
In 2020, 190 Training Institutes were being run by the State Police Forces. State-wise,
these institutes’ names, addresses, and contact numbers are given in Appendix-1. The highest
```
number of Training Institutes, i.e., twenty-four (24), is run by the Tamil Nadu Police, followed by
```
18 by the Madhya Pradesh Police.
UT TRAINING INSTITUTES
In 2020, a total number of 17 Training Institutes were being run by the UT Police. The
```
highest number of Training Institutes, i.e., seven (7), were being run by the J&K Police. The
```
names, addresses, and contact numbers are given in Appendix-1.
CAPF/CPO TRAINING INSTITUTES
During 2020, a total number of 104 Training Institutes were being run by the Central Armed
Police Forces/Central Police Organizations, out of which 25 were run by the BSF, followed by 22
```
by the CRPF (Appendix - 2 & 6).
```

PRESIDENT’S POLICE MEDAL/POLICE MEDAL FOR GALLANTRY
President’s Police Medal/Police Medals for Gallantry is awarded to Police Personnel to
execute the conspicuous act of gallantry in saving life and property or preventing crimes, or
```
arresting dangerous criminals. A total of 12 President’s Police Medals for Gallantry (PPMG) and
```
```
581 Police Medals for Gallantry (PMG) were awarded for outstanding performance of Police
```
Personnel from States/UTs/CAPFs and CPOs. Out of 581 Police Medals for Gallantry awarded in
2020, the highest number 238 PMGs, was awarded to the Jammu and Kashmir Police, followed
```
by 130 to the CRPF (Table No. 6.2.5).
